transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-07-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Rios (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood CSM), Anita Rao (Cascade Head of ML), Ben Carter (Platform Eng), Sofia Lopez (Product), Tommy Ng (SRE)

Auto-summary: QBR focused on cost and reliability. Action items: send cost model, share tuning guide, schedule benchmark.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, appreciate you making time for the QBR and health check, uh quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood, with Diego and Liam, and on your side?
[00:08] Anita: Hi yeah Anita here, head of ML at Cascade, Ben and Sofia and Tommy on call as well.
[00:12] Ben: hey all
[00:14] Diego: Hi team, Diego SE, I'll go deep on perf later.
[00:18] Maya: Great, quick agenda: usage trends, cost, reliability incidents, and recommendations + next steps. We'll keep it conversational.

[00:30] Liam: Jumping in real quick, just to call out renewal window — I think Cascade's annual commit comes up in September, right Anita?
[00:36] Anita: Yeah early September is our renewal window, procurement has to sign off by mid-August to make sure budget cycles align.
[00:42] Maya: ok good to know, we'll include that in next steps.

[00:50] --- Usage & Adoption ---
[00:52] Maya: So usage — over the last quarter we saw 38% growth in generated tokens across your main chat route, embeddings stayed fairly flat. Ben, does that match what you're seeing on your side?
[01:02] Ben: Yeah that's about right, most of the traffic spikes are coming from the new personalization feature Sofia shipped in May. It's pretty bursty, like morning peaks into the east coast.
[01:12] Sofia: The product team expected a ramp but the burstiness was higher than we modeled. Sorry we didn't give a better forecast earlier.
[01:19] Diego: One thing we noticed: the average seq length rose to 950 tokens in those personalization calls, which increases decode time non-linearly. Also the KV cache hits were lower than expected — might be a prompt framing issue or session reset frequency.
[01:32] Anita: Ah right we rotate session IDs every user action for privacy reasons, that probably ruins the KV cache. We can look at keeping session for short windows but need to balance privacy.
[01:42] Diego: Totally, we can show a config that keeps KV cache for N interactions and still maintains your privacy SLAs.

[01:48] --- Cost Conversation ---
[01:50] Maya: On costs, we saw a 52% increase in spend month-over-month tied to those seq-length spikes and also the fallback policy that routes to the larger model during congestion. We put together a cost breakdown — you'll get that after the call.
[02:04] Anita: Yeah that's why procurement flagged us, the invoice in June was unexpectedly high. Can you explain the fallback behavior?
[02:12] Diego: Sure — your routing policy currently falls back from the medium latency model to the high-quality variant during queueing; that helps maintain accuracy but at higher token costs. We recommended implementing a graceful degrade — e.g. lower max tokens and prefer a quantized variant before switching to the larger model.
[02:29] Ben: What's the quality delta if we go from full FP16 to the 4-bit quant profile? Our P0 flows are sensitive.
[02:36] Diego: From our evals on similar prompts, end-user regressions were minor for the personalization snippets — like a 2-4% drop in exact match but latency and cost improved 30-40%. We'll send the raw eval set and numbers.
[02:49] Sofia: That's promising, would like to see examples.

[02:52] --- Reliability / Incident Review ---
[02:54] Tommy: We also want to review the 2025-07-10 incident — we saw a spike in tail latency that lasted ~18 minutes and caused timeouts for some customer sessions.
[03:05] Diego: I pulled the traces — it looks like an autoscaler flapping event in your dedicated pool caused a transient queue growth, and the route fallback then pushed more load to the larger model which saturated some workers. There's also a small bug in the routing selector where the cooldown was too short.
[03:20] Anita: We captured some traces and logs, I'll share them. Any immediate mitigations?
[03:24] Diego: Short term we recommend tightening autoscaler thresholds and increasing cooldown to 90s, and enable prefix caching on the most common prompt templates. That should cut token decodes by about 15-20% during bursts.
[03:36] Tommy: We'll need a test plan for changing autoscaler thresholds — don't want to flip to too low and underprovision.
[03:42] Diego: Totally — we'll coordinate a staging run. We'll also put a canary with the new cooldown and monitor the queue length.

[03:48] --- Security & Compliance ---
[03:50] Maya: On compliance, you asked for SSO and KMS docs last time. We have updated SOC2 cert pack and KMS integration notes. We'll share the redacted audit summary and key rotation docs. Any additional items?
[03:59] Anita: SOC2 is good, procurement also wants to see SAML configuration examples and proof of HSM/backed KMS usage, and data residency confirmation for EU traffic.
[04:09] Maya: We'll include SAML guides and HSM/KMS note. For EU residency, traffic for eu- region is pinned — we'll give routing confirmations and the region SLA.

[04:18] --- Roadmap & Product Asks ---
[04:20] Sofia: On roadmap, we're planning to expand personalization to 20% more users by Q4. Any features from Redwood that help reduce cost for high-scale personalization?
[04:28] Diego: A few things: 1) smarter batching (we can use latency-headroom to batch async writes), 2) prefix caching for repeated boilerplate prompts, 3) quantization variants for non-critical responses, 4) fine-tuning a smaller condense model for retrieval-augmented flows. We'll send example configs and expected unit economics.
[04:44] Ben: For batching, what's the tradeoff to latency? We can't add >150ms p99.
[04:48] Diego: You can often batch within a 40-80ms window and keep p99 within target if you limit batch size. We have telemetry hooks so we'll propose a config aligned with your p99 goal.

[04:58] --- Pricing & Renewal ---
[05:00] Maya: Given the spend trend, we recommend reviewing a reserved capacity add-on for predictable throughput — Dedicated reserved nodes or a blended commit can reduce unit costs. We can model a 12-month commit vs pay-as-you-go.
[05:12] Anita: Procurement will want numbers. Also, are there termination or early-exit penalties for reserved capacity?
[05:18] Maya: We'll include standard contract language — there are options for overage credits and phased ramp to avoid cliff penalties. We'll put the full cost model and legal summary in the follow-up.

[05:28] --- Open Questions & Live Discussion ---
[05:30] Ben: Diego, can you run a quick demo of the KV cache config and show where we can reduce session resets?
[05:35] Diego: Yeah, quick share — so your library currently calls reset_session on every user click, if you instead maintain session_id for N interactions and clear PII at the application layer, the runtime will keep the KV cache and avoid re-encoding the prefix. That reduces compute by ~12-18% on our sample. (Note: demo referenced deck link: https://redwood.app/kv-cache-howto)
[05:52] Anita: There's a privacy constraint — we can't persist PII in the cache. Can the cache be ephemeral and encrypted with a per-tenant key?
[05:59] Diego: Yes, Redwood supports per-tenant encryption and KMS-wrapped keys; the cache can be ephemeral and destroyed after inactivity window. We'll document the exact flow.

[06:10] Sofia: For the fallback routing, can we prefer a quantized variant before promoting to a larger model?
[06:15] Maya: Yes that's the recommended policy; we can ship a routing policy that prefers the quantized-medium -> medium -> large sequence.

[06:22] --- Recap & Next Steps ---
[06:24] Maya: Quick recap: Redwood to send cost breakdown and committed vs PAYG models, Diego to send tuning guide and config examples, Cascade to confirm renewal window and provide traces from the July 10 incident. We'll schedule a 60-minute benchmark session in the next two weeks to simulate peak traffic.
[06:38] Anita: Sounds good, please include stakeholders in procurement and security.
[06:41] Maya: Will do. Any final questions?
[06:44] Tommy: One last — can we get an on-call contact for urgent infra during the benchmark?
[06:48] Liam: I'll be the CSM on-call for the benchmark, Diego will be technical point. We'll share contact details in the follow-up.
[06:55] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action item owners.
[06:59] Anita: Thanks everyone bye.

[07:00] End of meeting

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (names, acronyms) as typical of automated transcripts. References: KV cache howto link, cost model spreadsheet (to be attached), SOC2 and KMS docs (to be attached).
